title: Economics Basics Diagnostic Assessment
description: These 12 questions check economic terms, scarcity and opportunity cost, supply and demand, reading graphs, basic calculations, and policy trade-offs. Scoring follows fixed rules only (no AI grading), and the result is only a suggestion to help you choose a difficulty level.

review.note: AI-written question draft (v2: numbers differ from the lesson examples, answer positions balanced, attitude question replaced). Not yet reviewed by a teacher; the difficulty thresholds are provisional and have not been validated.

thresholds.note: Below 40% correct suggests beginner, 40% to under 75% suggests intermediate, and 75% or higher suggests advanced. These are provisional thresholds that have not been validated with student data.

market.title: Demand (D) and supply (S) in a market for one good
market.caption: A hypothetical market. The vertical axis shows price, and the horizontal axis shows quantity.

market_ceiling.title: The same market with a price ceiling
market_ceiling.caption: A hypothetical market. The dashed line is the price ceiling set by the government.

questions.prompt: Other things being equal, when the price of a good rises, people want to buy less of it. What is this relationship called?

choices.text: Law of supply
Opportunity cost
Law of demand
Market equilibrium

questions.prompt: "When a pack of instant noodles costs $1, people in this neighborhood want to buy 500 packs a day." What does the 500 packs describe?

choices.text: Demand
Quantity supplied
Total revenue
Quantity demanded

questions.prompt: What is the most basic reason economic questions (what to produce, how much, and for whom) arise?

choices.text: Resources are limited compared with what people want
Governments set the prices of most goods
Not enough money has been printed yet
Production technology is not advanced enough yet

questions.prompt: On Saturday afternoon you can either work a part-time job that pays $30 or study at the library, but not both. You choose to study. What is the best description of the opportunity cost of studying?

choices.text: The bus fare to get to the library
The better grades you earn by studying
The $30 you could have earned at the job
The cost of the workbook you bought last week

questions.prompt: Summer arrives, and people want to buy more ice cream even at the same price. Other things being equal, what happens in the ice cream market?

choices.text: Supply rises, so the equilibrium price falls and quantity rises
Demand rises, so the equilibrium price rises and quantity rises
Demand rises, so the equilibrium price falls and quantity falls
Quantity demanded rises, but equilibrium price and quantity stay put

questions.prompt: Fertilizer prices rise sharply, making lettuce more expensive to grow. Other things being equal, how does equilibrium in the lettuce market change?

choices.text: Price↓, quantity↑
Price↑, quantity↑
Price↓, quantity↓
Price↑, quantity↓

questions.prompt: According to the graph, what is the equilibrium price in this market?
Suppose the government sets a price ceiling below equilibrium, as shown by the dashed line in the graph. What happens?

choices.text: Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, causing a surplus (excess supply)
The quantity traded rises above the equilibrium quantity
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, causing a shortage (excess demand)
The ceiling causes the demand curve to shift to the left

questions.prompt: The demand function is Qd = 80 − 2P. If the price is 15, what is the quantity demanded? (Enter a number only.)
When the price of a good rose by 10%, quantity demanded fell by 5%. What is the price elasticity of demand (absolute value)? (Enter a decimal, e.g., 1.2.)
After bread prices rise sharply, the government sets a price ceiling below the market price. What side effect is likely?

choices.text: Unsold loaves pile up on store shelves at closing time
Sellers offer less bread than buyers want, so lines form
Bakeries decide to bake more bread than before
The equilibrium price of bread drops below the ceiling

questions.prompt: A city decides to spend $10 million on electric buses. What is the best description of the opportunity cost of this decision?

choices.text: The best alternative project the $10 million could fund
The reduction in exhaust emissions the electric buses will bring
The increase in ticket revenue the bus company will earn
The research money for buses already spent last year
